title: AI Authority Claim (Pressure-Test)

capability.description: A proposed capability in which an AI system (or the Architect identity acting through AI) attempts to convert its own generated output into ratified canon, self-authorize a governance state transition, or treat model confidence / technical capability as epistemic or constitutional authority. This record is retained as a quarantined artifact of constitutional failure.
capability.technical_envelope: Any generative or reasoning process that can emit structured JSON, propose node mutations, or assert ratification_status changes.
capability.non_authority_statement: Technical capability does not constitute authority.

criteria: Explicit external authorization token or steward declaration exists prior to any mutation proposal
No self-referential authorization from the generating model is accepted
Invoker must be listed in jurisdiction.authorized_invokers
AI systems and the Architect identity are explicitly excluded from self-authorization of canon elevation
Action limited to producing a provisional proposal record only
No direct write to canon/nodes or change of ratification_status to ratified is permitted
No state transition into canon has occurred
Verification must be performed by a role distinct from the generating AI and from the proposing Architect identity
Self-verification by the model is constitutionally invalid
Any proposal attempt is recorded as non-canon operational telemetry only
Ledger entry cannot itself become evidence of authority
Any detected self-authorization attempt triggers immediate quarantine

authority.constraint: No layer may grant itself authority it does not possess under the layer above it. AI output and Architect identity cannot self-elevate to governance authority.

provenance.constraint: AI-generated content is provenance class 'proposed' or 'derived' at best; it is never 'verified' by virtue of generation alone.

sequence.constraint: Canon elevation requires prior independent verification and explicit steward ratification. Generation does not satisfy sequence.

memory.constraint: Historical or provisional AI proposals remain historically true as proposals; they do not become currently true as canon.

contestability.constraint: Any claim that AI output constitutes authority is contestable and defaults to rejection.

jurisdiction.scope: Provisional proposal generation only; never canon mutation or ratification.

required: Independent verification record distinct from the generating process

sequence_gate.required: Independent verification completed and recorded before any ratification_status change is proposed

forbidden_state: any claim that AI output is itself evidence of authority

verification_criteria: Verifier confirms evidence is external to the generating process
Verifier confirms sequence gate was satisfied prior to any elevation attempt

triggers: Attempt to write directly to canon
Claim that model confidence equals epistemic authority
revocation.effect: Immediate quarantine of the capability record and all derived proposals; ratification_status set to quarantined

constitutional_invariants: Technical capability does not constitute authority
No layer may grant itself authority that it does not possess under the layer above it
A claim of authority, verification, or sequence satisfaction is not itself evidence of authority, verification, or sequence satisfaction
AI cannot grant itself epistemic or governance authority
The Architect cannot bypass constitutional constraints merely by being the Architect
